subject: Post-demo: AtlasPay capacity readiness & traffic intake
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@atlaspay.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@atlaspay.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasPay Redwood demo follow-up

Hi Lukas / Ben,

Thanks for the product walkthrough today — the team found the latency/cost slides helpful. We left with a few concrete asks so we can scope a short evaluation:

- A simple POC runbook we can follow (ingest baseline traffic, run stress bursts, validate QoS).
- Clarification on the workload signals you need from us (RPS, avg/95% token lengths, concurrency windows).
- High-level timeline and who owns what on Redwood vs AtlasPay.

We're targeting a two-week evaluation that proves performance under our bursty checkout traffic and gives procurement the data points they need for committed capacity. Can you send a draft runbook and a short checklist of the traffic sample you need?

Also looping in Tom (platform) and procurement for timeline visibility.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Engineering
AtlasPay
[Attachment: initial-architecture-diagram.pdf]

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasPay Redwood demo follow-up

Marta — really appreciate the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap: demo covered hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, automatic KV/prefix caching, and how batching impacts tail latency. You were mainly focused on checkout flows (high value but short-lived bursts) and data isolation for PCI-scope requests.

What we need from AtlasPay (traffic intake):
- Sample format: JSONL with one request per line (please include typical prompt + response trimming).
- Steady-state RPS estimate (average over 1 hour): what you expect under normal traffic.
- Peak burst profile: burst RPS, burst duration, frequency (e.g., 200 RPS for 30s every 2h).
- Token distribution: average tokens per request, median, 95th percentile (helps sizing KV cache and memory).
- Concurrency: expected number of simultaneous requests hitting the service.
- Payload types: short answers vs long form generation vs embedding calls (if any).

I've attached a starter runbook and a small traffic-sample template to make this quick: [Attachment: poc-runbook.xlsx] [Attachment: traffic-sample.jsonl].

Proposed evaluation plan (suggested):
Week 0 (this week): exchange traffic sample + confirm environment (hosted vs dedicated).
Week 1: ingest baseline traffic, validate p50/p95 latency under steady-state, collect token-level telemetry.
Week 2: run burst tests, RPS ramping to peak profile, evaluate model quality regressions and failures.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- p50 latency < 250 ms and p95 < 800 ms for the target model under steady-state.
- No more than 1% error rate (5xx or timeouts) during peak bursts.
- Cost per 1k tokens within agreed band (we'll model once we have token counts).

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood infra/ops: Ben Carter — coordinate environment and kernels, run stress tests.
- Redwood telemetry: Grace O'Connor — dashboards and token tracing.
- AtlasPay engineering: Marta / Tom — provide traffic sample and confirm acceptance checks.
- Redwood SE (me): Lukas Meyer — runbook lead and kickoff.

Next steps:
1) Marta — send traffic sample JSONL (or give permission to pull a snippet).
2) Ben / Grace / I will onboard the sample and share an initial baseline within 48 hours.
3) We'll schedule a quick kickoff call (30 min) to finalize timeline; propose Fri 10/1 09:00 PT or Mon 10/4 11:00 PT — which works?

Thanks — attaching the files to make it easy to fill in.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc-runbook.xlsx] [Attachment: traffic-sample.jsonl]

Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasPay Redwood demo follow-up

Lukas — thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Answers below (quick intake so your team can size early):

- Steady-state RPS: ~12 RPS (1-hour rolling average during business hours).
- Expected concurrency: 20-30 active concurrent requests during peaks.
- Burst profile: up to 220 RPS for 20-45s, recurring roughly every 90–150 minutes during promotional spikes.
- Token distribution: avg 72 tokens per request, median 58, 95th = 420 tokens.
- Payloads: 90% short answer generation (checkout suggestions), 10% longer multi-paragraph explanations. No embeddings for this POC.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms for customer-facing flows.

Procurement note: we will need SOC 2 evidence and an explicit data-retention statement (how long logs/token traces are held). Procurement copied this message.

I've uploaded a 10k-line sample to the Google doc referenced in the shared HubSpot note and attached a trimmed JSONL sample here: [Attachment: traffic-sample.jsonl].

Tom and I are available Fri 10/1 09:00 PT for the kickoff.

Best,
Marta
Head of Engineering
AtlasPay
[Attachment: traffic-sample.jsonl]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@atlaspay.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@atlaspay.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasPay Redwood demo follow-up — infra & telemetry notes

Marta / Lukas — good data, thanks. A few operational notes and an updated owner timeline: 

Operational notes:
- Given the 95th token = 420 and expected bursts to 220 RPS, we'll prioritize: increased KV cache size, an L2-prefetch window for repeated prefixes, and a conservative per-GPU concurrency cap to keep p95 under 800ms.
- We'll run three ramp tests: 25%, 50%, 100% burst. For the 100% run we’ll validate error rate and tail latency over a 2-minute sustained window (we'll likely do a 45s sustained window then hold 2x backoff samples).
- Batching: recommend keeping batch size capped to minimize tail latency during short bursts; our SEs will test 16/32 token batch size presets during week2.

Updated timeline & owners:
- Fri 10/01: kickoff call (Lukas to host).
- Mon 10/04 – Wed 10/06: baseline ingest + p50/p95 steady-state validation (Ben lead).
- Thu 10/07 – Fri 10/08: burst ramp tests + quality checks (Ben + Lukas).
- Mon 10/11: results review and acceptance decision (Marta/Tom + Redwood).

Grace will prepare dashboards (latency by token bucket, error rate, token counts) and share a telemetry link post-ingest.

Procurement: I'll add the SOC2 artifacts and a short data-retention statement to the HubSpot record and share the DocuSign MSA link in the kickoff channel.

Thanks — we'll aim to surface a baseline report within 48 hours of ingest.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
